newsitem.title: USA: Ill. plans $100 mln GO competitive sale on July 22.
newsitem.headline: Ill. plans $100 mln GO competitive sale on July 22.

text.p: Illinois plans to sell $100 million of general obligation debt competitively on July 22, a bond analyst for the state budget bureau said Tuesday.
Ilinois also expects to issue $150 million to $200 million of tax-exempt college savings bond debt in September or October, bond analyst Kurt Kauffman said.
The July issuance will be the first by the state for fiscal 1998 with a standard offering structure of equal principals over 25 years, Kauffman said.

The issuance includes about $55 million for Capital Facilities needs, $15 million for Transportation, B-Mass Transit and Public Airport Facilities purposes and $30 million for Anti-Pollution purposes, according to a preliminary official statement.
The bonds will have a federal tax exemption, but not a state exemption, Kauffman noted.
Illinois has requested ratings from Moody's Investors Service, Standard & Poor's and Fitch Investors Service.
Chapman & Cutler is serving as bond counsel and sealed bids will be received until 1200 EDT at the Capital Development Board Room in the James R. Thompson Center in Chicago.
